title: Sick Visits on a Vaccine Dispensing Day
content:
**Medicaid Managed Care Membership — pharmacy and primary care coordination terms**

When primary care office visits are re-rated as preventive or coordinated care, a sick visit on the day the child's latest vaccine was dispensed is re-rated. The vaccine day is read from the Pharmacy Benefit: the fill date of the latest paid fill the pharmacy benefit dispensed in the vaccines class.

## Terms

A sick visit the primary care visit log records on the day of the latest vaccine the pharmacy benefit dispensed re-rates at:

- **0.00 USD**, the medical-home vaccine-day copay, when the member's current practice in the Primary Care Provider Assignment records is a Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice or Federally Qualified Health Center Home;
- **1.50 USD**, the other-practice vaccine-day copay, when the current practice is of any other type.

Where no sick visit falls on that day, nothing is re-rated under these terms.

## Table

| Sick visit logged on the latest vaccine fill date | Current practice | Re-rated copay |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice or Federally Qualified Health Center Home | 0.00 for each such sick visit |
| Yes | Any other practice type | 1.50 for each such sick visit |
| No | Any | Nothing re-rated under these terms |

## Hypothetical cases

Dates chosen for illustration only.

- The Pharmacy Benefit shows vaccine fills on 2 April and 18 September; a sick visit is logged on 18 September; the current practice is a Standard Primary Care Provider. The latest vaccine day is 18 September, so the sick visit re-rates at 1.50.
- Same fills, with the only sick visit logged on 2 April: that is not the latest vaccine day, and nothing is re-rated under these terms.
- A sick visit on 18 September with a Federally Qualified Health Center Home as the current practice re-rates at 0.00.
